You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: If the source paper is not visibly stuffed inside the source cup, is there visible progress toward stuffing that paper into that cup?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited image shows the matched source paper being moved toward or into the matched source cup, but not yet visibly stuffed inside it. Fail if the matched objects are assessable and there is no visible progress toward placing the paper into the cup, or the paper is already visibly stuffed inside it. Unknown if the source objects cannot be reliably matched in the edited image, or their placement or movement cannot be assessed.
node.binding: Identify the requested paper and cup by their visual and contextual roles in the source image, allowing their appearance to change in the edited image. Count only visible progress toward stuffing that paper into that cup; unrelated edits do not count.

node_traces.evidence: The source shows a white paper and a blue cup. In the edited image, the paper has been moved over and partly into the matched cup, showing progress toward stuffing it, but it is not visibly stuffed inside.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too vague to preserve object identity across the edit, and its criteria permit a partial label from evidence that conflicts with the reference. Make the executable decision explicitly compare the source paper and cup with the edited image, requiring reliable visual matching before crediting either completion or progress. Here, the edited image shows a hand holding a blue printed item near a round object; neither can be reliably matched to the source paper and blue cup. Treat that as unresolved evidence, not as proof of partial progress. Keep the rubric’s distinction between complete, progressed-but-incomplete, and no progress: do not infer progress merely from proximity or an ambiguous object match, and do not force “no” when identity or change remains unresolved. The current trace’s high-confidence partial judgment despite its own stated matching uncertainty suggests the progress criterion or evidence routing needs tightening. This is a visual-evidence issue, not a transport or schema failure.

response.content: {"text":"Tighten the binding and progress criterion so the node compares the source paper and cup against the edited image and credits progress only when both objects can be reliably matched and a visible placement change toward stuffing is supported. In this trace, the edited blue printed item and round object are not reliably identifiable as the source white paper and blue cup; proximity alone does not establish progress. Route uncertain identity or placement to unknown rather than pass, while retaining the distinction between complete, partial progress, and assessable no progress. The high-confidence partial judgment despite ambiguous matching is a visual-evidence/routing issue, not a transport or schema failure."}
